\[
N=3^2\cdot 7^2\cdot 11^2\cdot 13^2\cdot 19^2\cdot 61
=(3\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot19)^2\cdot61
=57057^2\cdot61
=3255501249\cdot61
=198585576189.
\]
It is odd because every prime factor is odd.

Primality of the listed primes is direct: \(3,7,11,13,19,61\) are prime; for \(61\), trial division by \(2,3,5,7\) suffices since \(\sqrt{61}<8\).

Exact divisor-sum computation:
\[
\sigma(3^2)=13,\quad
\sigma(7^2)=57=3\cdot19,\quad
\sigma(11^2)=133=7\cdot19,
\]
\[
\sigma(13^2)=183=3\cdot61,\quad
\sigma(19^2)=381=3\cdot127,\quad
\sigma(61)=62=2\cdot31.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sigma(N)=13\cdot57\cdot133\cdot183\cdot381\cdot62
=426027470778.
\]
Also
\[
2N=2\cdot198585576189=397171152378.
\]
Thus
\[
\sigma(N)-2N=28856318400\neq0,
\]
so this candidate does not survive condition 3.

The reason it is the strongest best-effort candidate is that if \(22021\) were incorrectly treated as prime, then \(\sigma(22021)=22022\), and the original Descartes number
\[
3^2\cdot7^2\cdot11^2\cdot13^2\cdot22021
\]
would satisfy \(\sigma(N)=2N\). The obstruction is exactly the certified factorization \(22021=19^2\cdot61\), since
\[
\sigma(19^2\cdot61)=381\cdot62=23622
\]
instead of the spoof value \(22022\). In exact ratio form,
\[
\frac{\sigma(N)}{2N}=\frac{11811}{11011}
=\frac{3\cdot31\cdot127}{7\cdot11^2\cdot13}.
\]
Hence no exact certified candidate survives the checks; the submitted object is the best-effort certified factorization found.
